text:
sasha: Hey team — customer jane_customer reports a billing mismatch. Their client SDK estimator shows ~38k tokens for a long streaming chat with a function call, but the invoice shows ~112k. Request id c-98712 included. Any quick suspects? :eyes:

miguel: Do we have the raw request payload + whether they used streaming close vs a normal end-of-stream? streaming truncation often causes client-side tokenizers to miss the final chunks.

jane_customer: @sasha attaching the sanitized payload below. We did streaming and then called the tool. We stop the stream on our side after receiving the function name and args (we close the ws), so maybe something is left on your end?

sasha: paste: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/chat/completions \n -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \n -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n -d '{"model":"open-ghost-11b","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize logs"}],"functions":[{"name":"extract","parameters":{}}] }'```

ingrid: two quick notes: 1) when clients cut a TCP/WS connection mid-stream we still finish generating server-side and that output can include metadata tokens (KV/cache, tool return prefixes). 2) function return payloads often include structured JSON with lots of punctuation that tokenizers count differently.

miguel: Also check if they used the SDK estimator that only counts final tokens (post-delta merge) vs our meter which counts every generated delta + any internal prefix tokens we inject for routing/fallback. That can multiply counts when many intermediate deltas are emitted.

jane_customer: we used the local JS estimator shipped in @redwood/js-sdk v0.8.4 with the default streaming handler. We never enabled captureAllDeltas.

sasha: OK. hypothesis: client estimator saw early stop after function name and args were streamed and closed connection — they didn't see the trailing tool/assistant finish which we still generated and billed. That trailing output includes the function wrapper and a KV prefix for session that we add (e.g., session metadata + tool provenance). That could explain ~3x.

ingrid: To confirm we need server-side meter breakdown for c-98712 (token buckets: prompt, streaming-deltas, function-return, injected-prefix). @billing-bot can you attach the meter breakdown for that request id?

billing-bot: Attached: meter snapshot for c-98712 — prompt: 4,200; deltas (stream chunks): 35,600; function_return: 52,100; injected_prefix: 20,300. Total: 112,200. (internal only)

miguel: There we go. The estimator the customer used only counted prompt + visible deltas until they closed; it did not account for the function_return and injected_prefix which are generated after their client closed the stream.

jane_customer: Is there a best practice? We can't keep clients connected indefinitely.

sasha: Short-term: tell them to reproduce without streaming (stream:false) for billing parity — server finalizes and client sees same tokenization. Medium-term: we should add an SDK option `includePostcloseTokens` or `captureAllDeltas` that captures server-final chunks even if the app triggers an early close, or emit a final small event before client closes so estimator sees the full output.

ingrid: Action items: 1) Support — ask customer for full ws logs + exact SDK version (assigned: sasha). 2) Engineering — evaluate emitting an explicit `finalized` chunk before we allow client to drop connection; research adding a metering header + optional client-visible signature of final token count (assigned: miguel). 3) Billing — consider a short window refund policy for early disconnect anomalies and add recommendation docs (assigned: billing team).

miguel: Quick repro steps for eng: reproduce with streaming + function call; on server, log token buckets and simulate immediate client disconnect after function name chunk; confirm server still generates function_return/injected_prefix. Provide script.

sasha: I'll ask the customer for logs and offer to run a non-streaming replay to compare. put customer expectations: we can run audit and propose credit if the extra tokens were emitted after an early disconnect and not avoidable on their side. :+1:

jane_customer: Thanks — sending logs now. Appreciate the clarity and recommended workaround.

sasha: thanks team, marking follow-up for next-day.
